CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient ID: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Sex: Male (fetal tissue)
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Analysis of fetal tissue post-pregnancy loss. Suspected chromosomal abnormality as cause of fetal demise.

SPECIMEN
Uncultured placental tissue

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured placental material to detect aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y. Multiple polymorphic microsatellite markers were amplified for each chromosome using fluorescently labeled primers. Fragment analysis was performed by capillary electrophoresis. Peak area ratios were calculated to determine chromosome copy number. Triploidy screening was included.

RESULTS

CHROMOSOME 16: ABNORMAL - MOSAIC TRISOMY 16
Informative markers analyzed:
- D16S682 (16q12.1): Triallelic pattern with peak ratios 1:1:1 in ~50% of cells
- D16S492 (16q12.2): Triallelic pattern with peak ratios 1:1:1 in ~50% of cells  
- D16S485 (16q22.2): Triallelic pattern with peak ratios 1:1:1 in ~50% of cells

Mosaicism detected: Normal diploid cell line and trisomy 16 cell line present
Estimated proportion of trisomy 16 cells: ~50%

OTHER CHROMOSOMES:
Chromosome 13: Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome 14: Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome 15: Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome 18: Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome 21: Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome 22: Normal disomic pattern

SEX CHROMOSOMES: XY (Male)
No evidence of sex chromosome aneuploidy

TRIPLOIDY SCREEN: Negative

INTERPRETATION
This QF-PCR analysis reveals mosaic trisomy 16 in the placental tissue, with approximately 50% of cells showing trisomy 16 and 50% showing a normal chromosome complement. All other chromosomes tested (13, 14, 15, 18, 21, 22, X, Y) show normal copy number.

Mosaic trisomy 16 is a well-recognized cause of pregnancy loss. The presence of mosaicism suggests that the trisomy 16 arose as a meiotic error followed by post-zygotic loss of one chromosome 16 in a subset of cells (trisomy rescue), creating the normal diploid cell line. Complete trisomy 16 is incompatible with life, but mosaic forms may allow survival to later gestational ages.

The finding of mosaic trisomy 16 provides a likely explanation for the pregnancy loss. This is typically a sporadic event with low recurrence risk.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these findings and their implications
2. While this appears to be a sporadic event, parental chromosome analysis (karyotyping) may be considered for reassurance, as a parental balanced rearrangement involving chromosome 16 cannot be completely excluded based on QF-PCR alone
3. The recurrence risk for mosaic trisomy 16 is generally low (<1%) in the absence of parental chromosome rearrangements
4. Prenatal diagnosis options should be discussed for future pregnancies

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
